Ontario Casino Revenue Hits Record as Sports Betting Falls 30%

Published September 25, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Ontario's regulated online gambling market posted CA$396.3 million in total gaming revenue for August, according to iGaming Ontario's monthly report covered by Casino.org and IntergameOnline — down about 4% from July's total, but with casino and sports betting moving in sharply opposite directions underneath that headline number. Online casino revenue climbed to CA$336.3 million, up roughly 2% month over month and now accounting for about 85% of the province's total regulated gaming revenue, while online sports betting revenue dropped 30% to CA$54.4 million.

The numbers behind the split

Total wagering across the province came in at CA$9.740 billion, down about 1% from July's CA$9.884 billion. Casino handle made up the overwhelming majority of that at CA$8.776 billion, a 90% share of all wagering, and casino's share of net revenue was even more lopsided at 85%. Sports betting handle, by contrast, fell 15% month over month to CA$843 million and produced just CA$54.4 million in revenue — a 14% share of the province's total, down 30% from July. Peer-to-peer poker remained the smallest segment, at CA$5.6 million in revenue, up about 6%. Active player accounts fell to 1.208 million in August, down 11% from July, though average revenue per active account rose 8% to CA$328.

Enforcement actions in the same report

iGaming Ontario's report also referenced several recent enforcement actions by the province's gaming regulator, the AGCO, against licensed operators: a CA$120,000 fine against Betty Gaming for age-verification failures, a CA$70,000 fine against Booming Games over a prohibited auto-play feature, and a CA$100,000 fine against NorthStar Gaming for anti-money-laundering shortcomings. Separately, Fanatics was noted as having received regulatory approval to operate in the province.

Why it matters

Ontario remains the largest regulated online gambling market in Canada, and the widening gap between its casino and sports betting segments is a trend worth watching for any operator or bettor tracking the broader North American market: casino games continue to be the more consistent revenue driver for most regulated operators, while sports betting revenue tends to swing harder from month to month based on the sports calendar and betting outcomes. August sits in a relative lull between the summer sports calendar and the NFL and college football season ramping up, which likely contributed to the sports betting pullback, but a 30% single-month drop is a notably sharp swing even accounting for seasonality.

Sources

  • Casino.org — "Ontario Sports Betting Revenue Plunges 30% in August as Casino Sets Record"
  • InterGame Online — "Online casino drives Ontario igaming revenue up in August"
